newsitem.title: INDIA: India 96/97 sugar output seen at 14 mln tonnes.
newsitem.headline: India 96/97 sugar output seen at 14 mln tonnes.

text.p: India's sugar output in the 1996/97 (October-September) season is forecast at 14.0 million tonnes, down from 16.4 million in the previous season, Food Minister Devendra Prasad Yadav said on Thursday.
"Sugar production in 1996/97 is not likely to be as high as it was last year. It is however still likely to be of the order of about 14 million tonnes," Yadav told a meeting of parliament deputies.
The Indian Sugar Mills Association (ISMA) also last week forecast the 1996/97 sugar output at 14 million tonnes.
Yadav said sugar production in 1996/97 had been adversely affected due to financial problems faced by sugar mills and late-start crushing by factories.
Yadav said the 1996/97 sugar season had started with an inventory of eight million tonnes.
He said the ex-mill price of levy sugar would be announced at an early date.
Levy price is the rate at which the government buys sugar from millers for sale through the public rationing system. The mills have to contribute 40 percent of their output to the government as levy.
